text.p: These are the highlights in the Bosnian press on Tuesday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Bosnian Serb Dusan Tadic was sentenced to 20 years by the International Criminal Tribunal for former Yugoslavia in The Hague. Tadic was found guilty on nine counts of persecution and murder.
- News of Tadic's sentence was received by Bosnians with relief but also with resignation, the paper says, because the main perpetrators are still at large.

- As long as all those responsible for organising genocidal campaign in Bosnia are not brought before the tribunal, the notion of collective guilt will prevent reconciliation and the implementation of the Dayton peace agreement, says Mirza Hajric, aide to the Bosnian presidency chairman.

- Equipment needed for establishing telecommunications links between the Moslem-Croat federation and the Serb entity has arrived in Bosnia, say sources in the Council of Ministers. But the deadline set by the international community for beginning integration of the Bosnian telephone network expires on Tuesday.
- At least a month is needed to connect the main telephone lines between the entities and an additional two weeks for testing, source in state postal and telephone company says.

- Chairman of the Bosnian presidency, Alija Izetbegovic met on Monday with a military delegation headed by General Rasim Delic. The army officers briefed Izetbegovic on an organizational scheme for the new Moslem-Croat federation army.
- Foreign trade minister Hasan Muratovic and the Malaysian ambassador to Bosnia, Rastam Mohd Issa, signed an agreement for Malaysian training for Bosnian air controllers.

- The office of High Representative to Bosnia says the recent NATO operation in Prijedor had no connection with the constitutional crisis in the Serb entity and the Bosnian Serb president's decision to dissolve the national assembly.
- The High Representive's office said unspecified measures may have to be taken to prevent the Serb media from spreading ethnic hatred and those measures will be announced soon.
- Federation institute of statistics reports that average salary in the Moslem-Croat federation in May was 261 German marks, which represents a 2.2% increase from April.
- Foreign trade minister Hasan Muratovic says the international donors' conference for Bosnia will be held by the end of July without a doubt, probably between July 23 and 29.
- Bosnian Serb president Biljana Plavsic continues "crusade" against corruption and for "establishment of a legal state."
- Plavsic said that Miroslav Toholj, general manager of the Serb television, should be sacked for his lack of professionalism. --Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864
